open_points.subject: R0-07 bootstrap success output
open_points.text: “the success message shows the normalized email to the operator who supplied it”
open_points.question: What exact email-normalization rule and output contract—message format and stdout/stderr destination—define the newly promised bootstrap success message?
options: Trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the complete address; emit a stable message on stdout
Normalize only the domain or apply additional Unicode/IDNA rules; emit implementation-defined text
Treat the message as human-only output with no stable format or stream
open_points.default_guess: Trim whitespace, lowercase the complete address, and emit a stable single-line success message on stdout.

witness.initial: No staff account exists, and the bootstrap operator supplies ` Alice@Example.COM `.
events: The host operator runs the local bootstrap command successfully.
outcomes: The command displays `Alice@example.com`, or sends the message to stderr.
witness.observer: The host operator and any deployment wrapper capturing command output

open_points.subject: R0-24 progress read versus viewer read-only guarantee
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version” conflicts with “all viewer capabilities are read-only; a viewer can never mutate data” and “Archived projects expose the same reads in read-only mode”
open_points.question: Is creation of the empty manual budget considered an allowed internal side effect of a viewer's progress read, or must the read-only guarantees prevent a viewer request from causing that stored change?
options: A viewer progress read creates the budget despite the read-only guarantees
Only a mutation-capable staff read may create it; a viewer read remains side-effect-free
No progress read may create stored state for an archived project
open_points.default_guess: Treat the creation as a narrowly named internal side effect allowed for every otherwise-authorized progress reader, and narrow the read-only guarantees accordingly.

witness.initial: An archived project has an active viewer grant and no budget record.
events: The viewer enters with a valid access link.
The viewer reads the project's progress.
outcomes: R0-24 creates a persistent empty manual budget because the progress read is authorized.
The viewer read creates nothing because viewer capabilities and archived reads are read-only.
witness.observer: The viewer on a later budget read, staff inspecting the project, and the audit/storage boundary

open_points.subject: Authorization for progress-triggered budget creation
open_points.text: “Every operation on a project's records … checks … required capability” and “reading the progress … creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: Which capability authorizes the budget creation hidden inside a progress read: progress-read capability alone, budget-mutation capability as well, or a system-owned action independent of the caller's mutation capabilities?
options: Progress-read capability authorizes both the response and automatic creation
Budget-mutation capability is additionally required
The system performs creation independently after authorizing only the read
open_points.default_guess: Authorize the request with progress-read capability and classify the creation as a system side effect attributed to the authenticated reader.

witness.initial: A principal may read progress for an archived project but has no budget-mutation capability; the project has no budget.
outcomes: The read succeeds and creates the empty budget using only progress-read authority.
The request is refused, or succeeds without creation, because the principal lacks budget-mutation authority.
witness.observer: The requesting principal and an administrator inspecting the project's budget

open_points.subject: Meaning of project “has no budget yet”
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: What exact persisted state counts as having no budget: no budget version of any kind, no active budget version, or no manual budget version?
options: No manual or snapshot budget version exists
No budget version is currently active
No manual budget exists, even if an imported snapshot exists
No usable budget exists after considering activation and mappings
open_points.default_guess: Create the empty manual budget only when the project has no manual or imported budget version at all.

witness.initial: An archived project has an accepted imported snapshot, but no budget version has been activated.
events: An authorized actor reads project progress.
outcomes: No manual budget is created because an imported budget record already exists.
An empty manual budget is created because the project has no active budget.
witness.observer: The reader and staff later reviewing available budget versions

open_points.subject: State of the automatically created manual budget
open_points.question: What stored facts define that version—especially its identity, activation status, ordering/version position, creation provenance, and whether it becomes the project's active budget?
options: Create and immediately activate a uniquely identified empty manual version
Create an inactive manual version requiring later activation
Create a singleton implicit manual budget with no ordinary version identity
open_points.default_guess: Create one ordinary, uniquely identified manual budget version and make it active only when the project has no active budget.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget and an authorized actor reads progress.
events: The portal creates the empty manual budget.
The actor subsequently reads the budget summary or lists budget versions.
outcomes: The summary reports an active manual budget with zero sections.
The project still reports budget unavailable while an inactive or implicit empty version exists.
witness.observer: The progress reader and staff reviewing budget versions

open_points.subject: Failure and concurrency semantics of progress-triggered budget creation
open_points.text: “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: What must the progress read return if creation fails, and what guarantees prevent concurrent or repeated reads from creating multiple empty manual versions?
options: Creation and read are atomic; failure returns an explicit storage error, and concurrent reads converge on one version
The progress read may succeed even if creation fails; a later read retries
Each qualifying read may create a separate empty version
Creation is idempotent by a project-level singleton constraint
open_points.default_guess: Make creation and the read atomic, enforce one automatically created empty manual version per project, and return an explicit storage failure if it cannot be persisted.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget, and two authorized sessions can read its progress.
events: Each request observes the initial no-budget state before either creation commits.
outcomes: Both requests converge on one empty manual budget version and succeed.
Two empty manual versions are created, or one request fails with an unspecified conflict.
witness.observer: The two callers and staff later listing or activating budget versions
